# Workflow and work plan

Mermaid diagrams are written as text in `{mermaid}` cells, so they can be versioned and reviewed like the rest of the report. Cell options use the `%%|` prefix, and a `fig-` label makes them cross-referenceable.

## Analysis workflow

@fig-workflow summarises the reporting pipeline used in this template.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-workflow
%%| fig-cap: "Analysis and reporting workflow."
%%| fig-width: 6.2
flowchart LR
  A[Raw data] --> B[Processing<br/>Python / R]
  B --> C{Validated?}
  C -- yes --> D[Figures and tables]
  C -- no --> B
  D --> E[Quarto report]
  E --> F[PDF via Typst]
  E --> G[HTML]
```

## Work plan

@fig-gantt shows the project schedule. It is drawn by `code/python/gantt.py` from the table in `data/workplan.csv`, so updating the plan means editing that file (also possible in a spreadsheet program). Work packages take shades of the primary colour, completed tasks are faded and milestones are shown as diamonds.

```{python}
#| label: fig-gantt
#| fig-cap: "Project work plan. The dashed line marks the reporting date."
#| fig-alt: "Gantt chart of three work packages over 2026 with tasks, two milestones and a line marking the reporting date."
import sys
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sys.path.insert(0, "code/python")
from gantt import gantt

fig = gantt("data/workplan.csv", today="2026-11-17")
plt.show()
```

Other layouts: `scale="quarter"` for long projects, `scale="project"` for project months (M1, M2, ...), and `highlight="WP2 Experiments"` to emphasise one work package.
